record.question: A 53 year old male patient is admitted with COPD. The nurse notes that he has neck vein distention and slight peripheral edema. These signs indicate the onset of:
record.explanation: Answer B: Cor- pulmonale. Neck-vein distension and peripheral edema in COPD suggest right-sided heart strain/failure (cor pulmonale). Source/context note: Clinical evaluation is required; edema/JVD are not specific to cor pulmonale. Reference: https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/copd. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
